nodes.label: Agent Lifecycle States (working / departed)
nodes.rationale: Agents are labeled 'working' or 'departed'; the panel bar counts 7 departed. Finished workers stay visible on the wall (dimmed, transcript preserved) rather than disappearing, keeping an audit trail of completed work.

nodes.label: impl-task-1 Agent
nodes.rationale: Worker agent on claude-sonnet-5, status 'departed' after completing 'Implement Task 1 scaffo...'; transcript shows edit/test/commit loop ending in a SendMessage status report and an approved shutdown_request.

nodes.label: impl-task-2 Agent
nodes.rationale: Worker agent on claude-sonnet-5, status 'departed' after 'Implement Task 2 catalog'; transcript shows tests (14/14 passing), a git commit, and a SendMessage 'STATUS: DONE commit SHA' report back to the team lead.

nodes.label: Per-Agent Message Input
nodes.rationale: Each column has its own prompt ('message team-lead', 'message impl-task-1'), letting the operator steer any individual agent directly without going through the lead.

nodes.label: Panel Bar Keyboard Controls
nodes.rationale: Terminal-style keyboard-first control surface: select, open, esc interrupt, x stop, ^T tasks, plus current selection ('team-lead 68%', '7 departed'). The console behaves like a TUI-in-the-browser aimed at fast operator intervention.

nodes.label: team-lead Agent
nodes.rationale: Orchestrator agent on claude-opus-5, status 'working', 68% context used (680k/1M), ~$94.52 api-equiv. Runs on the larger model and accounts for nearly all session cost, implying a design where an expensive lead delegates implementation to cheaper sonnet workers.

nodes.label: Live Tool-Call Transcript Stream
nodes.rationale: Each column renders a condensed feed of tool invocations (Bash, Read, Edit, Write, ToolSearch, WebFetch, SendMessage) with truncated one-line results, glyph-coded (bullet for calls, corner for results, x for errors, check for successes). Optimized for scanning activity at a glance rather than reading full output.

nodes.label: View Modes (wall / overview / tasks / rail / grid)
nodes.norm_label: view modes (wall / overview / tasks / rail / grid)
nodes.rationale: Five alternative projections of the same team session, suggesting the console separates session data from presentation so the operator can choose density vs. detail.

nodes.label: NEEDS YOU Attention Bar
nodes.rationale: A dedicated queue ('NEEDS YOU · 0 nothing waiting') for items blocked on human input, so the operator does not have to scan every column to find agents waiting on them.

nodes.label: SendMessage Team Coordination
nodes.rationale: Workers report completion to the team lead via SendMessage ('STATUS: DONE commit SHA...', 'Message sent to team-lead') and request shutdown via a shutdown_request that the lead approves ('Shutdown approved'). Coordination and lifecycle transitions are message-driven rather than implicit.

nodes.label: Token and Cost Tracking
nodes.rationale: Every agent header shows a context-usage progress bar, percent, tokens/limit (e.g. 680k/1M), and an api-equivalent dollar figure; the top bar aggregates the team (149.0M tokens, ~$97.77, 1h 14m). Makes spend and context pressure first-class monitoring signals per agent and for the whole session.
nodes.source_location: top bar and each column header

nodes.label: Wall View Layout
nodes.rationale: Side-by-side vertical columns, one per agent, each streaming that agent's live tool-call transcript. Lets a single operator watch an entire multi-agent team at once instead of switching between sessions; active agent columns are bright while departed agents are dimmed to push attention toward live work.

nodes.label: Workflow Bar Shed Order
nodes.rationale: Ruling 18: totals, then elapsed, then taskId - lower survives longer, mirroring the team bar's precedent that identity outlives figures. The task id is the one metric not re-derivable from the view below; totals go first because the agents view carries them in full. The shed mechanism moved into the shared Bar so both modes shed, each with its own order. Measured: with all three shed the bar's remaining furniture still costs 741.48px.

nodes.label: Run-Picker Trigger Width Bound
nodes.rationale: Ruling 19: min(236px, 26vw) with the name ellipsised and the runId and caret never shrunk. Two terms because one number cannot serve both ends: 236px is what the 1180px design width can spare; 26vw covers the narrow end where 741.48px of un-sheddable furniture leaves at most 27.79% of a 700px frame. A max-width and never flex-shrink - every bar child is flex: none, and a shrinkable one would wrap and double the bar's height. A half-drawn runId identifies nothing.

nodes.label: /console Command
nodes.rationale: Always replaces the running server rather than reporting a healthy one as fine: the server is detached and outlives its session, so claude plugin update leaves the OLD build serving on 4823 and a health check answers ok either way. Restarting is cheap because the console rebuilds its screen from its own append-only log. Kills by PORT, not plugin path - a path match once killed only the installed build while four locally-built servers accumulated, one of them happily answering /health. Starts the installed build regardless of whether a team is live, and reports a no-team start plainly so an empty wall does not read as broken.

nodes.label: /console-setup Command
nodes.rationale: Once-per-machine setup for the two keys the plugin manifest cannot carry: the env pair and subagentStatusLine. It merges and never overwrites, checks the machine first (claude pinned at 2.1.231 internals, node 22+, plugin installed), shows the exact keys and waits for an explicit yes - never on a teammate's say-so - backs settings.json up, validates it parses afterwards, and reverses itself on request. It never writes hooks (a copy in settings.json would post every event twice) and never touches statusLine unasked. settings.json over a shell profile because it is per-machine and reaches editor-launched sessions.

nodes.label: Seven-Part Dispatch Contract
nodes.rationale: Every dispatch prompt carries: the task (TaskGet, claim via TaskUpdate), the goal in one sentence, the skills to use, scope (files owned and off limits), verification commands, the terminal deliverable stated in full, and close-out (TaskUpdate to completed plus a report). Parts 1, 3 and 6 are the ones that get dropped.

nodes.label: implement-task-list Skill
nodes.rationale: Turn session-identified work into shared-list tasks, then hand each to a teammate that owns it from unread to open PR. Core principle: the lead delegates the work AND the paperwork - a teammate that does not claim its own task, invoke its own skills, and open its own PR is a pair of hands, not an owner, and the lead becomes the bottleneck. Seven-step pipeline including verifying the roster in config.json before teammates get deep, because a wrong roster is cheap to fix in the first minute and expensive after six agents have edited files.

nodes.label: Four-Field Task Contract
nodes.rationale: Every TaskCreate carries subject (imperative, names the outcome), description (executable by someone who never read the conversation - exact values, exact paths, the why behind arbitrary-looking constraints), blockedBy (set afterwards via TaskUpdate, real dependencies only), and metadata { complexity, model, effort, why } - the field that gets skipped, and required.

nodes.label: to-agents-task-list Skill
nodes.rationale: A task list is a delegation contract, not a to-do list: each task is picked up by an agent with none of this conversation's context, possibly in parallel, possibly on a different model. That needs a description that stands alone, dependencies that are real, and a model sized to the task. Closes with a table, notes, and one direct ask (adjust models / adjust tasks / start the work) - a message stopping after the table leaves the contract unsigned.

nodes.label: Agent Teams Console
nodes.rationale: A Claude Code plugin that renders a live browser console for agent teams: every teammate's transcript, the shared task list, mailboxes, context burn, and NEEDS YOU items. Never started manually - the plugin's PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks on the Agent and Workflow tools start the server and print the URL once per team. Everything is local: nothing leaves 127.0.0.1 and cross-origin requests are refused.

nodes.label: Agent Teams Env Vars
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 (without it there are no teams to show) and CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 (fills the tasks view). They live in settings.json because a plugin manifest has nowhere to put env, and a shell export only reaches sessions started from that shell. Read once at session start, so a restart is required.

nodes.label: Per-Team Append-Only Event Log
nodes.rationale: agent-teams-console/logs/<team>.jsonl, one file per team so a console started for a second team cannot overwrite the first team's history. Pruned at startup, capped per event kind and per agent for transcript history, dropped after a week untouched. Only mostly rebuildable: roster, transcripts, tasks and mail come back from ~/.claude on the next sweep, but hook-pushed data (status line, per-agent substatus, permission and plan cards) exists nowhere else. A one-time migration folds the old shared events.db into per-team logs, renaming it to events.db.migrated-<epoch-ms>.

nodes.label: Idle Reaper Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: The server exits ten minutes after the last team goes away and immediately on the lead's SessionEnd. The reaper reads only the filesystem and keeps the process alive while any team has two or more members. 'The server stays up' is a description, not a mandate.

nodes.label: Ten Observation Hooks
nodes.rationale: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, UserPromptSubmit, Notification, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreCompact - all registered in plugin/hooks/hooks.json and firing from the plugin, so permission cards, plan approvals and tool activity work on a bare install with no settings.json edit. Each costs one refused connection while the console is not running.

nodes.label: subagentStatusLine Key
nodes.rationale: The settings.json key that reports each teammate's current tool into its console header. No plugin-manifest equivalent exists, so /console-setup writes it - but only when the key is absent.

nodes.label: Team Mode (six views)
nodes.rationale: Six views: wall (one transcript column per teammate, lead pinned left), overview (context-occupancy tiles), comms (everyone room plus per-pair inbox threads), tasks (shared task list), rail (keyboard-navigable list with one big transcript), grid (six panes for wide monitors).

nodes.label: Workflow Mode
nodes.rationale: Chosen by what triggered the run, not a toggle. A workflow subagent never enters members[], so a workflow is not a team: no roster, no inboxes, no task list, no composer. Four views: run, agents, script, journal. It has no controls and cannot have any: skip-agent and stop-run are an AbortController.abort() plus an in-memory registry write inside the session process; nothing on disk drives them, the per-session unix socket carries no workflow verb, a queued prompt would arrive only after the run ends, and a signal to the pid would kill the whole session. A control whose only effect is its own highlight teaches a capability that does not exist. Checked against Claude Code 2.1.231.

nodes.label: Console Decisions Log
nodes.rationale: The tie-breaker over the self-contradicting design bundle: where a design document and this file disagree, this file wins, and a reopened question needs a new row rather than a component change. Precedence: the CHANGELOG's newest entry usually governs; the prototype (turn 4a for team mode, 6a/7a otherwise) governs where prose is silent; a measured argument beats an aesthetic one; standing rule 1 always holds. 19 rulings recorded.

nodes.label: Design Bundle (agents-team-ui-docs)
nodes.rationale: agents-team-ui-docs/design/: README.md, CHANGELOG.md, MESSAGING.md, and the Octo Session Console prototype (dc.html). Lives in an unversioned sibling repository because the design folder is a re-pulled mirror of a Claude Design project - versioning it here would record someone else's edit history. It contradicts itself in about twenty places; read the newest-first CHANGELOG first when implementing against it.

nodes.label: Unified Chat Bubble Grounds
nodes.rationale: Ruling 7a: one colour pair for both rooms - left speaker neutral-900 fill / neutral-800 edge / neutral-200 text, right speaker accent-700 fill / accent-600 edge. accent-900 with inset accent-500 is the selected-row tint everywhere else, so a bubble on it reads as a selection; the chosen pair measures 5.6:1. One constant consumed by both rooms so they cannot drift, same reasoning as max-width: 64%.

nodes.label: Context Warning Threshold Formula
nodes.rationale: Ruling 2: the ! warning fires on the displayed percent, tokens/contextLimit >= 0.75, because a configurable '75%' that lights at 63% on screen is a setting the operator cannot verify. The note fires halfway from the threshold to compactAt and reports distance to compactAt in tokens. No model in catalog.json inverts the two stages (compactAt is 83.5% of 200k, 96.7% of 1M).

nodes.label: PR Field Refused, Diffstat Shipped
nodes.rationale: Ruling 17: the picker row carries +N/-M for what is uncommitted against HEAD; nothing names a PR. gh is optional, a forge API needs a token and per-forge client which a local read-only console has none of, and refs/remotes/*/pull/* exists only if hand-fetched.

nodes.label: Quiet Metadata Register
nodes.rationale: Small quiet metadata text (column headers, footers, meta/hint lines, key legends, empty states, timestamps, receipts, read-only markings, the composer glyph) is --color-neutral-600 with a 10px floor, not target - measured contrast on --color-bg: neutral-700 is 2.69:1, neutral-600 is 4.09:1; contrast beats taste. Text already at 10.5/11px stays; match neighbours in the same pane. Does NOT cover neutral-700 used as a status/state colour or as border/shadow/gutter tokens - recolouring those would be standing rule 2's mistake in the other direction.

nodes.label: Read-Only Column Marking
nodes.rationale: Ruling 15: every non-lead wall column and the rail's non-lead pane carry a read-only marking, though the prototype draws none. Without it, a column with no composer is indistinguishable from one whose composer failed to render. Ruled by the team lead during the one-composer close-out.

nodes.label: Respawn Card Kept
nodes.rationale: Ruling 12: the failure card's respawn control ships because it is backed by POST /api/agents/{name}/respawn - a lead-inbox write (src/server/http.ts:374). The card names what the call does (asks the lead to respawn the teammate) and must never imply the console restarts a process.

nodes.label: Standing Rule 1: No Control Without a Runtime Call
nodes.norm_label: standing rule 1: no control without a runtime call
nodes.rationale: A control that names no runtime call does not ship. It removes controls with no backing call; a control whose call exists is rule 1 obeyed, not evaded (ruling 12 kept respawn because POST /api/agents/{name}/respawn is a real lead-inbox write).

nodes.label: Standing Rule 3: No Field Without a Source
nodes.norm_label: standing rule 3: no field without a source
nodes.rationale: A field with no data source is blank for every operator, and nobody reports a blank. Grounds for ruling 17: the PR field was refused because a local read-only console makes no forge API calls and .git/config yields the repo, never the pull request; diffstat scoped to uncommitted work because branch-against-base means guessing main.

nodes.label: Standing Rule 4: Prototype Contradiction vs Predating Prose
nodes.norm_label: standing rule 4: prototype contradiction vs predating prose
nodes.rationale: Do not write what the prototype does not do - but the rule guards against prose the reference build contradicts, not prose it predates. Ruling 15 kept the read-only markings the prototype never drew: it was drawn before the single-composer model existed, so its silence is an absence, not a disagreement, and the newest voice governs.

nodes.label: Shared-Checkout Isolation
nodes.rationale: Never pass isolation: 'worktree' when spawning a teammate - it routes the Agent call down the ordinary-subagent path and what comes back never enters members[], gets no TaskGet/TaskUpdate, has no mailbox, and never appears in the console; nothing errors. Isolation comes from disjoint file ownership named in the dispatch prompt: each teammate stages its own paths by name (never git add -A), one shared branch created by the lead (they share HEAD, so git checkout -b moves everyone), never fix another teammate's file, retry on index lock.

nodes.label: Terminal Deliverable Settlement
nodes.rationale: Opening a PR is outward-facing, so an agent will correctly refuse it by default and end at 'committed on your branch' - the single most common way the workflow ends half-finished. Ask once before dispatching, for the whole batch, and state the answer explicitly in every dispatch prompt; per-teammate or unstated is how three branches land and two sit unpushed.

nodes.label: Real Dependencies Only
nodes.rationale: blockedBy means cannot start, not would-rather-do-second. Real: the blocker produces a type, field, route, file or decision the blocked task reads. Verification is blocked by everything that can break it. A decision task blocks whatever the decision changes - model open questions as their own tasks. Every needless blocker is serialized time.

nodes.label: Size by Decisions, Not Lines
nodes.rationale: The verbs in the description you just wrote are the evidence - no separate analysis pass. Mechanical (exact outcome, typecheck proves it) gets haiku/low; standard (one layer, repo precedent to copy) gets sonnet/medium; judgment (decide/design/contract other tasks consume) gets opus/high. Escalate to xhigh/max only when judgment-level AND expensive to unwind. A 400-line mechanical port is haiku; a 12-line change to a type every module imports is opus. If you can't size it, split it.

nodes.label: Launcher Wake Gate
nodes.rationale: The launcher runs on every Agent or Workflow tool call, so it is written to be cheap and do nothing almost every time. For an Agent call it reads ~/.claude/teams/<team>/config.json and gives up unless two or more members are listed; every Workflow call wakes the console since a run forms no team. Ordinary subagents, Explore, workflow fan-outs and parallel search agents never appear in members[] (verified in a capture spike with six live workflow subagents), so they cost one short-lived shell process and nothing else.

nodes.label: plugin/ Install Boundary
nodes.rationale: Everything that ships lives in plugin/ (1.3M); nothing else in the repo is installed. claude plugin install runs npm install when it finds a package.json at the plugin root - an earlier layout put 141M on disk that way - so package.json and src/ stay at the repo root. plugin/dist/ is committed because a plugin is just files and nothing builds on the user's machine; the esbuild bundle has no runtime dependencies and the build is deterministic.

nodes.label: Status Line Non-Takeover Policy
nodes.rationale: The console's statusLine command ends in printf '' - it draws nothing, its job is only to POST the payload. Written over an existing status line (ccstatusline, starship, custom) it would blank the bar, so the install never takes the key unless it is empty; the operator gives up only the rate-limit gauge and the lead's cost/context readouts. Chaining both (POST then hand payload to the user's command) happens only on an explicit request.
